title: Multi-word streaming column-sum for n greater than 64
description:
Implement the multi-word streaming column-sum path that extends `permanent_bipedal3` to $n > 64$, per the R3 cache-blocking design.

## Background

For $n > 64$ the column-sum vector spans multiple `u64` pairs. The R3 design doc (`60c30e2d`, attached) prescribes cache-blocked streaming over chunks tuned to fit Zen 3 L1d (32 KiB), with the inner loop walking down the toggled column word-by-word and updating each `column_sum[w]` chunk via `Bipedal3::add`/`sub`.

This issue lands `permanent_bipedal3_multiword` covering $n \in \{65, \ldots, 255\}$. The single-word path (T9) remains the fast path for $n \le 64$; dispatch to multi-word kicks in only when needed.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal3_multiword(matrix: &Bipedal3Matrix) -> Fp<3>` exists and supports $64 < n \le N_{\max}$ with $N_{\max}$ documented in the function doc-comment.
- [ ] [hard] Memory layout matches the R3 doc (column-major); cache-blocking parameters are documented constants tied to the L1d size.
- [ ] [hard] Multi-word output matches `permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>` (T7) under two layered cross-checks: (i) the multi-word code path is directly verified bit-identical to `permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>` on at least 850 random matrices spanning $n \in \{2, 5, 8, 16, 20\}$ in the fast tier (release mode skips the `debug_assert!(n > 64)`, allowing the multi-word code path to run at any $n \le N_{\max}$); (ii) for the originally-targeted $n \in \{65, 72, 96, 128\}$, at least 5 block-diagonal matrices each, `[A_{n_0} \oplus I_{n - n_0}]` with $n_0 \in \{10, 11, 12\}$, so the permanent factorises algebraically to `permanent_ryser(A_{n_0})`; these tests carry `#[ignore = "sim: large-n cross-check"]` because the $2^n$ Gray walk is infeasible at those $n$, and their bodies document the oracle so they remain valid against a faster machine. The reformulation is unavoidable because `permanent_ryser` itself caps at $n \le 63$ (so it cannot directly oracle $n \ge 65$), and the $2^n$ Gray walk at $n \in \{65, 72, 96, 128\}$ requires $10^{10}$ s or more on a single core.
- [ ] [hard] `permanent_bipedal3` dispatches to the single-word path for $n \le 64$ and the multi-word path otherwise; the dispatch is transparent to callers. `gray_code_iter` widens its bound to `u128` so the $n = 64$ boundary is well-defined.
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes (the unignored fast tests remain under 5 s each).

## Amendment history (2026-05-11)

- Criterion 3 reformulated: ryser at $n \ge 65$ is infeasible (ryser caps at $n \le 63$, and the $2^n$ Gray walk takes $> 10^{10}$ s). Replaced with layered (small-n direct + large-n block-decomposable) cross-checks. Detailed in attached doc `dev/active/a7886bd8-amendments-2026-05-11.md`.
- Criterion 4 clarified: `n = 64` routes to singleword via `u128`-widened `gray_code_iter`.
- `N_MAX_MULTIWORD = 255` (was 256, which would have indexed `c[4]` in `gray_counter_is_zero_above`).
